title: Yehudah bar Nechemyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Menachot 68b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.68b), Rabbi Tarfon was sitting and struggling with a question. Yehudah bar Nechemyah said before him, “No; if you say—” Rabbi Tarfon fell silent, and Yehudah bar Nechemyah’s face beamed. Rabbi Akiva said to him: “Yehudah, your face beamed because you answered an elder? I wonder whether you will live long.” Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai said: “It was in the period leading up to Passover. When I went up for Atzeret, I asked about him, and they told me that he had passed away.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: אותו הפרק refers to that time, not a chapter of a book; פרס הפסח is the period before Passover, not a “breaking of the Passover” or a Passover-offering chapter. No exact number of days is added. Atzeret here is Shavuot. The initial refutation is abbreviated with a dash in Hyman; the missing legal argument is not supplied. ר״ט and ב״נ are resolved from the full names in the same passage, and ר״ע is supported here by the full name Rabbi Akiva in the exact cited passage. The account reports the admonition and later death without a newly asserted causal explanation. The printed סח: conventionally gives 68b; the complete matching Davidson Hebrew passage has now been checked.

Menachot 68b:12–14 explicitly supplies Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehudah berabbi Ilai in the same exchange. Hyman’s bare Yehudah bar Nechemyah remains bare, even though a later sentence of the Davidson text adds Rabbi to that name. The period before Passover and Atzeret are temporal references; Hyman’s abbreviated legal argument remains abbreviated. The statement reports the admonition and subsequent death, without adding causation or an exact interval.
